correctness.rationale: The source-backed geometric identification reduces the claim to all 80 nonisotropic affine 2-planes of a symplectic F2^4. The quadratic second-difference identity gives inclusion in a five-congruence kernel; explicit basis images prove the kernel has index 128; sixteen enumerated incidence vectors have exact determinant +128, so span equals kernel. The pure-standard-library checker proves all finite assertions using integer operations, with an independent integer Smith-form cross-check (1^11,2^4,8). The conclusion applies uniformly to every specified Kummer quartic; it does not extrapolate from sample curves.

originality.rationale: The exact nonisotropic Rosenhain incidence congruence and order-eight node obstruction do not follow from the geometric classification of the 80 tetrads, from classical Picard-lattice results, or from the prior isotropic Göpel incidence lattice. Searches of the named tetrad lattice, full primary geometrical sources and published related incidence problems located no identical integral result; unrelated coding tables remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: The exact integral Smith form may be tabulated in older binary-code, design or symplectic-geometry work under a different terminology, despite no such match in checked material.

The closest published Göpel theorem makes this a motivated complementary calculation; whether it constitutes a substantive separate research contribution is a value judgment supported here by the different exponent and sharp eightfold reconstruction boundary.

value.rationale: The 80 Rosenhain tetrads form a natural geometric 4-subset system on the 16 nodes. The complete integral saturation criterion and exact order-eight obstruction measure whether a formal node combination can be assembled from these geometric units. It is not equivalent to rational span or to the previous Göpel computation, whose quotient has exponent four despite the same index 128. This contrast gives a natural and usable invariant for integral configurations without claiming to compute the Picard group.
